title: Methods
text: Treat set S factors held observed values coalition, value v(S) = f_t(x_S^1, x_{N \setminus S}^0). Shapley value factor marginal effect averaged every coalition factors: \phi_i = \sum_{S \subseteq N \setminus \{\}}   \frac{|S|!\,(n - |S| - 1)!}{n!}\,\bigl[v(S \cup \{\}) - v(S)\bigr]. allocation efficient (shares sum \Delta Y_t), symmetric (interchangeable factors get equal shares), additive, gives zero factor never changes outcome. Interactions split evenly. example , outcome 10 + 5a + 3b + 2ab. Factor gets main effect plus half interaction, factor b gets treatment:
code: rt <- make_run_table(c("a", "b")) rt[, y := 10 + 5 * a + 3 * b + 2 * a * b] decomp_algebra(rt, list(summary_vars = "y", decomp_vars = c("a", "b"),                         decomp_method = "shapley")) #>    measure     a     b #>     <char> <num> <num> #> 1:       y     6     4

what: Das Gupta’s standardization is the same thing
title: Methods
text: Das Gupta’s symmetric standardization, classical demographic tool, weights marginal effect 1 / \bigl[n \binom{n-1}{k}\bigr], k = |S|. Expanding binomial gives \frac{1}{n \binom{n-1}{k}} = \frac{k!\,(n-1-k)!}{n \cdot (n-1)!} = \frac{k!\,(n-k-1)!}{n!}, Shapley weight. binary factors two methods identical, package implements one weight formula. method = "das_gupta" accepted deprecated alias "shapley".

title: Get started
text: vignette uses small SIR epidemic two interventions: beta_reduction, prevention programme cuts transmission 50%; treatment_effect, treatment speeds recovery. scale linearly 1990 2020. model object holds fixed structure, parameters hold inputs decomposition vary. split matters, shapleydecomp modifies params.
code: create_sir_model <- function(population = 1e5, years = 1990:2020) {   structure(     list(population = population, years = years,          S0 = population - 10, I0 = 10, R0 = 0),     class = "sir_model"   ) }  create_sir_params <- function(years = 1990:2020) {   yrs <- as.character(years)   list(     years            = years,     base_beta        = 0.3,     gamma            = 0.1,     beta_reduction   = setNames(seq(0, 0.5,  length.out = length(years)), yrs),     treatment_effect = setNames(seq(0, 0.15, length.out = length(years)), yrs)   ) }

title: Get started
text: Four methods required.
code: run_simulation.sir_model <- function(model, params, ...) {   n <- length(model$years)   S <- I <- R <- inf <- deaths <- numeric(n)   S[1] <- model$S0; I[1] <- model$I0; R[1] <- model$R0   for (t in 2:n) {     yr    <- as.character(model$years[t])     beta  <- params$base_beta * (1 - params$beta_reduction[[yr]])     gamma <- params$gamma + params$treatment_effect[[yr]]     inf[t]    <- beta * S[t - 1] * I[t - 1] / model$population     deaths[t] <- 0.01 * I[t - 1]     rec       <- gamma * I[t - 1]     S[t] <- S[t - 1] - inf[t]     I[t] <- I[t - 1] + inf[t] - rec - deaths[t]     R[t] <- R[t - 1] + rec   }   data.table::data.table(year = model$years, infections = inf, deaths = deaths) }  summarize_results.sir_model <- function(model, sim_output, ...) sim_output  get_baseline_value.sir_model <- function(model, params, factor_name, cf_type,                                          baseline_year, ...) {   if (cf_type == CF_TOTAL_IMPACT) return(list(type = "zero"))   list(type = "change_since",        value = params[[factor_name]][[as.character(baseline_year)]]) }  build_counterfactual.sir_model <- function(model, params, factor_name,                                            decomp_year, cf_type,                                            baseline_values, ...) {   idx <- params$years >= decomp_year   params[[factor_name]][idx] <-     if (cf_type == CF_TOTAL_IMPACT) 0 else baseline_values[[factor_name]]$value   params }

code: res <- shapley_decompose(   model, params,   factors      = c("beta_reduction", "treatment_effect"),   summary_vars = c("infections", "deaths"),   decomp_years = 2000:2020,   cf_type      = "total_impact",   verbose      = FALSE ) names(res) #> [1] "decomp"          "step_scenarios"  "extended_decomp" "run_table"       #> [5] "run_summary"     "params" head(res$decomp) #>    decomp_year    measure beta_reduction treatment_effect #>          <int>     <char>          <num>            <num> #> 1:        2000 infections      -1.620383                0 #> 2:        2000     deaths       0.000000                0 #> 3:        2001 infections      -1.942431                0 #> 4:        2001     deaths       0.000000                0 #> 5:        2002 infections      -2.288005                0 #> 6:        2002     deaths       0.000000                0 tot <- sequential_totals(res) tot[measure == "infections" & year %in% c(2005, 2010, 2020)] #>     year    measure beta_reduction treatment_effect #>    <int>     <char>          <num>            <num> #> 1:  2005 infections      -8.174118        -4.777467 #> 2:  2010 infections     -25.006188       -20.046996 #> 3:  2020 infections    -151.623899      -147.868569 inf <- tot[measure == "infections"] op <- par(mar = c(3, 4.5, 1, 1)) averted <- -t(as.matrix(inf[, .(beta_reduction, treatment_effect)])) colnames(averted) <- inf$year barplot(averted, col = c("#3b6ea8", "#d08c2b"), border = NA, las = 1,         ylab = "Infections averted", ylim = c(0, max(colSums(averted)) * 1.1),         legend.text = c("Prevention (beta_reduction)", "Treatment"),         args.legend = list(x = "topleft", bty = "n")) par(op) off <- res$step_scenarios[step_year == 1999, .(year, infections)] obs <- run_simulation(model, params)[, .(year, observed = infections)] chk <- merge(merge(inf, obs, by = "year"), off, by = "year") chk[, gap := beta_reduction + treatment_effect - (observed - infections)] max(abs(chk$gap)) #> [1] 1.136868e-13

title: Run a full decomposition analysis — shapley_decompose
text: model S3 model object. Must methods run_simulation(), summarize_results(), build_counterfactual(), get_baseline_value(). params Model parameters (model-specific list/object). factors Character vector factor names decompose. summary_vars Character vector summary variable names (columns output summarize_results()). decomp_years Integer vector years perform decomposition (e.g., 2000:2023). method Character, decomposition method. "shapley" (default) supported. "das_gupta" accepted deprecated alias: Das Gupta's symmetric standardization special case Shapley value binary /factors, weights identical. cf_type Character, counterfactual type: "change_since" (default) — counterfactual value baseline year; "total_impact" — counterfactual zero / intervention. baseline_year Integer, reference year "change_since" counterfactuals. Defaults min(decomp_years). decomp_scalar Numeric, lower bound factor levels run table. Default 0 (binary /). extended Logical, whether compute extended factor decomposition (effects output years >= decomp year). Default TRUE. step_scenarios Logical, whether compute step scenarios (-time series per decomp year). Default TRUE. verbose Logical, print progress messages. Default TRUE. n_cores Integer, number cores parallel counterfactual simulation runs. Default 1 (sequential). Values > 1 run every counterfactual simulation, across decomp years, one parallel::mclapply() map, cores 2^n runs single year can used. Windows support forking, falls back sequential warning. group_vars Character vector columns output summarize_results() identify independent groups, locations draws, decomposed separately. Default none. future_policies Character, every factor decomp year coalition run. "" sequential Shapley specified (Carter, "Estimating impact public health policies ... Shapley value decomposition", Algorithm 1): step y policies y observed values, policies y counterfactual, year-y policy varies across coalitions. attribution step y marginal impact year-y policy conditional past undiluted future, sequential_totals() sums steps factor's total impact every year. default. "" (behaviour version 0.2.0, kept reproducing old runs) leaves factor "" coalition observed values years, including y; -year attribution equals ""'s causal model, extended_decomp rows (year > decomp year) include future policies must summed across steps. ... Additional arguments passed model methods.

code: # A stock that decays by 20% a year and receives input x: # s_t = 0.8 * s_{t-1} + x_t run_simulation.stock_model <- function(model, params, ...) {   s <- as.numeric(stats::filter(params$x, 0.8, method = "recursive"))   data.table::data.table(year = params$years, stock = s) } summarize_results.stock_model <- function(model, sim_output, ...) sim_output get_baseline_value.stock_model <- function(model, params, factor_name,                                            cf_type, baseline_year, ...) {   list(type = "zero") } build_counterfactual.stock_model <- function(model, params, factor_name,                                              decomp_year, cf_type,                                              baseline_values, ...) {   params$x[params$years >= decomp_year] <- 0   params }  # Warm start: restart from the observed stock at the end of # warm_start_year and simulate only the remaining years supports_warm_start.stock_model <- function(model, ...) TRUE get_warm_start_state.stock_model <- function(model, sim_output, year, ...) {   s <- sim_output$stock[sim_output$year == year]   # Before the first simulated year there is no stock yet   if (length(s) == 0) 0 else s } run_from_warm_start.stock_model <- function(model, warm_state, params,                                             output_years, warm_start_year,                                             ...) {   s0   <- get_warm_start_state(model, warm_state, warm_start_year)   keep <- params$years > warm_start_year   s <- as.numeric(stats::filter(params$x[keep], 0.8, method = "recursive",                                 init = s0))   data.table::data.table(year = params$years[keep], stock = s) }  for (g in c("run_simulation", "summarize_results", "get_baseline_value",             "build_counterfactual", "supports_warm_start",             "get_warm_start_state", "run_from_warm_start")) {   .S3method(g, "stock_model", get(paste0(g, ".stock_model"))) }  params <- list(years = 2000:2010, x = rep(1, 11)) warm <- shapley_decompose(structure(list(), class = "stock_model"), params,                           factors = "x", summary_vars = "stock",                           decomp_years = 2000:2010,                           cf_type = "total_impact", verbose = FALSE)  # The same model without warm starts gives the same answer .S3method("supports_warm_start", "stock_cold", function(model, ...) FALSE) cold <- shapley_decompose(structure(list(), class = c("stock_cold",                                                       "stock_model")),                           params, factors = "x", summary_vars = "stock",                           decomp_years = 2000:2010,                           cf_type = "total_impact", verbose = FALSE) all.equal(warm$decomp, cold$decomp) #> [1] TRUE

title: shapleydecomp 0.3.0
text: package renamed decomposer shapleydecomp. CRAN already hosts DecomposeR, CRAN package names case-insensitive. API otherwise unchanged: replace library(decomposer) / decomposer:: shapleydecomp. decompose() renamed shapley_decompose(), longer masks stats::decompose(). arguments return value unchanged. exported functions documented examples. two new vignettes, Get started Methods, pkgdown site. New group_vars argument shapley_decompose() (group_vars run_decomp() params) names columns, location, identify independent groups. replaces hard-coded ihme_loc_id grouping. warm-start methods documented together ?warm_start, runnable example. documentation now describes actual contract: run_from_warm_start() receives observed simulation warm_start_year. n_cores > 1 Windows falls back sequential warning instead failing. Shapley algebra now single weight-matrix product groups, years measures (#8). 200 draws groups, full shapley_decompose() run 5-7x faster decomposition step alone 130x faster, results identical rounding. counterfactual runs, across decomp years, go one parallel map, decomposition longer limited 2^n cores time held slowest run year; future_policies = "", -run step y reused -run step y - 1 rather simulated (one run fewer per contiguous year); “every factor y + 1” parameters built per year (per worker) rather per run. Outputs identical previous version. Factors whose counterfactual leaves step’s parameters unchanged, programme started yet, detected null players. effect step 0, coalitions differ null factors simulated (#10). run reused confirming parameters identical(), model whose counterfactuals interact loses saving, never correctness. new run_summary output reports, per decomp year, runs simulated reused null factors. failed simulation inside n_cores > 1 now stops decomp year run failed, instead later, unrelated-looking error. summarize_results() (prepare_decomp()’s full_summary) may return data.frame. converted data.table way (#6). run_decomp(), decomp_algebra() decomp_pair() match rows /combinations factor values, row order longer matters (#7). Incomplete duplicated combinations, factor values 0/1, now error instead silently wrong result. decomp_pair() returns data.table measure first, like decomp_algebra() (#4). make_run_table() now prints called top level. shapley_decompose() reports progress message() instead cat().
